Q:final:1:o3: The state or territory WHS regulator
Q:final:2:p: The AS 2359 series of Australian Standards relates to:
Q:final:2:e: AS 2359 covers powered industrial trucks — forklifts.
Q:final:3:p: Your supervisor gives you a verbal instruction you don't fully understand. You should:
Q:final:3:e: Use questioning to confirm the instruction before you start.
Q:final:3:o1: Ask questions to confirm what is needed before starting
Q:final:3:o2: Do what you think they meant
Q:final:3:o4: Wait until the end of the shift
Q:final:4:e: Warning lights and signs at doorways and intersections are traffic warning systems.
Q:final:4:o4: Flashing warning lights at a doorway
Q:final:5:p: PPE sits where in the hierarchy of control?
Q:final:5:e: PPE is the least effective control — the last line of defence.
Q:final:6:p: Which of these is an overhead hazard?
Q:final:6:e: Powerlines, low beams and doorways can be struck by the mast or load.
Q:final:7:p: Why should you avoid driving on recently backfilled ground?
Q:final:7:e: Backfilled ground may not be compacted and can collapse under the forklift.
Q:final:7:o2: It may collapse under the weight of the forklift
Q:final:7:o4: It is always a pedestrian area
Q:final:8:p: You're moving sheets of plywood outdoors on a very windy day. The main risk is:
Q:final:8:e: Large flat loads catch the wind like a sail and can become unstable.
Q:final:8:o1: The load catches the wind and becomes unstable
Q:final:9:p: What is a sensible response to working in extreme heat?
Q:final:9:e: Drink water, take breaks and watch for heat stress; use sun protection outdoors.
Q:final:9:o2: Remove your seatbelt to stay cool
Q:final:9:o3: Drink water, take breaks and watch for heat stress
Q:final:10:p: A traffic management plan is used to:
Q:final:10:e: It separates people and vehicles and sets routes, speed limits, crossings and signage.
Q:final:10:o2: Separate pedestrians and vehicles and set routes and speed limits
Q:final:11:p: During the pre-start you find a crack at the heel of a tyne. You should:
Q:final:11:e: A cracked tyne is a serious defect. Tag the forklift out and report it.
Q:final:11:o1: Use the forklift for light loads only
Q:final:11:o2: Tag it out of service and report it
Q:final:11:o4: Continue and report at the end of the shift
Q:final:12:p: During operational checks you hear a grinding noise from the mast. You should:
Q:final:12:e: Unusual noises are a sign of a fault — stop, tag out and report.
Q:final:12:o2: Keep working and see if it stops
Q:final:12:o4: Stop, tag it out and report it
Q:final:13:p: Who may remove an "Out of service" tag from a forklift?
Q:final:13:e: Only an authorised person, once the repair has been completed and checked.
Q:final:13:o1: Only an authorised person once the repair is done and checked
Q:final:13:o2: Any operator who needs the forklift
Q:final:13:o3: The person who found the fault, after lunch
Q:final:13:o4: Anyone, if the supervisor is away
Q:final:14:p: The service brakes fail while you are travelling. What should you do?
Q:final:14:e: Take your foot off the accelerator, warn others with the horn, steer clear of people and obstacles, and use the park brake to stop.
Q:final:14:o2: Raise the load to slow down
Q:final:14:o3: Warn others with the horn, steer to a safe area and use the park brake to stop
Q:final:14:o4: Accelerate to get to the parking bay
Q:final:15:p: The temperature gauge shows the engine is overheating. You should:
Q:final:15:e: Stop and shut down safely, let it cool, and report it. Never open a hot radiator cap.
Q:final:15:o1: Open the radiator cap straight away
Q:final:15:o2: Stop, shut down, let it cool and report it
Q:final:15:o3: Keep driving to cool it with airflow
Q:final:15:o4: Pour cold water on the engine
Q:final:16:p: For the forklift to stay stable, the combined centre of gravity must stay:
Q:final:16:e: It must stay within the stability triangle.
Q:final:17:p: Where do you find a forklift's rated capacity?
Q:final:17:e: The rated capacity is on the manufacturer's data plate.
Q:final:18:p: A pallet holds 50 cartons of 20 kg each. The pallet weighs 25 kg. What is the total load weight?
Q:final:18:e: 50 × 20 = 1,000 kg, plus the 25 kg pallet = 1,025 kg.
Q:final:19:p: Which document records a load's weight measured at a weighbridge?
Q:final:19:e: A weighbridge docket shows the measured weight.
Q:final:20:p: You're using a jib attachment. What extra hazard must you manage?
Q:final:20:e: A load hanging from a jib can swing — move slowly and smoothly; capacity depends on hook position.
Q:final:21:p: Before using a rotator attachment to tip a load, you should:
Q:final:21:e: Rotating shifts the centre of gravity — keep the load low and the forklift stationary.
Q:final:21:o1: Raise the load to full height
Q:final:21:o3: Keep the load low and the forklift stationary
Q:final:22:p: Driving an unloaded forklift down a ramp, you should:
Q:final:22:e: Unloaded, keep the tynes pointing downhill: drive forwards down the ramp.
Q:final:22:o3: Drive forwards down with the tynes pointing downhill
Q:final:23:p: During a trial lift the rear wheels start to feel light. You should:
Q:final:23:e: The forklift is near its tipping point — lower the load straight away and reassess.
Q:final:23:o2: Lower the load straight away and reassess
Q:final:23:o3: Have someone sit on the back
Q:final:24:p: Why must you turn the charger off before disconnecting a forklift battery?
Q:final:24:e: Disconnecting while charging can create a spark, which could ignite hydrogen gas.
Q:final:24:o1: To avoid a spark that could ignite hydrogen gas
Q:final:25:p: After parking at the end of the shift, what else should you do?
Q:final:25:e: Do a post-operational check, then record and report any defects found during the shift.
Q:final:25:o1: Leave the key in for the next operator
Q:final:25:o4: Record and report any defects from the shift
Q:final:26:p: A pallet holds 6 layers of 5 cartons. Each carton weighs 20 kg and the pallet weighs 20 kg. What is the total weight?
Q:final:27:p: A running sheet lists a load as 2.5 t. How many kilograms is that?
Q:final:28:p: An evenly loaded crate 1,100 mm deep weighs 2,200 kg and sits hard against the backrest. The forklift is rated at 2,500 kg at a 600 mm load centre. Can it lift the crate?
Q:final:28:e: Load centre = 1,100 ÷ 2 = 550 mm — within 600 mm. 2,200 kg is less than 2,500 kg. OK to lift.
Q:final:28:o1: Yes — load centre 550 mm, and 2,200 kg is within 2,500 kg
Q:final:28:o2: No — the load centre is 1,100 mm
Q:final:29:p: A forklift is rated at 2,500 kg. Which ONE of these loads is within its rated capacity?
Q:final:29:e: 45 × 50 = 2,250 kg + 30 kg pallet = 2,280 kg — within 2,500 kg. The others are 2,600 kg, 2,600 kg and 2,530 kg — all over.
Q:final:29:o2: Two pallets of 1,300 kg each, lifted together
Q:final:29:o3: 45 cartons of 50 kg on a 30 kg pallet
Q:final:29:o4: A 2,500 kg crate on a 30 kg pallet
Q:final:30:p: The forklift's rated capacity is 1,300 kg. The pallet weighs 25 kg and each carton weighs 25 kg. What is the most cartons you can load?
Q:final:31:p: A forklift has touched a powerline. When is it safe to go back to it?
Q:final:31:e: Only once the electricity network operator confirms the power is off. Until then, stay at least 8 m away.
Q:final:31:o1: As soon as the mast is no longer touching the line
Q:final:31:o3: Only when the electricity network operator confirms the power is off
Q:final:32:p: Which of these is a HAZARD rather than a risk?
Q:final:32:e: An oil spill is a hazard — something that could cause harm. The chance of skidding on it, and how bad that would be, is the risk.
Q:final:32:o2: An oil spill on the forklift's route
Q:final:32:o3: How serious an injury could be
Q:final:32:o4: The likelihood of the load falling
Q:final:33:p: When you assess a risk, which two things do you consider?
Q:final:33:e: Risk = likelihood (how likely is harm?) and consequence (how bad would it be?).
